chunks: One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht al-Basri, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi al-Bilad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mihran, all from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, who said:

We were in Medina, and Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. So I said, 'Shaving it is preferable,' and Zurara said, 'Plucking it is preferable.' So we sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he permitted us while he was in the bathhouse waxing; he had already waxed his armpits. So I said to Zurara, 'Do you suffice with that?' He said, 'No, perhaps he did this for what is not permissible for me to do.'

He said, 'In what are you?' So I said, 'Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it; I said shaving is preferable, and he said plucking is preferable.' He said, 'You have hit the Sunnah and Zurara erred. Shaving it is preferable to plucking it, and waxing it is preferable to shaving it.' Then he said to us, 'Go and get waxed.' We said, 'We did that three days ago.' He said, 'Repeat it, for waxing is a cleanser.'
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for removing armpit hair according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the scholarly debate between Zarrara and the narrator regarding armpit hair removal, establishing a clear hierarchy: waxing (al-itala') is superior to shaving, which in turn is superior to plucking. The Imam further clarifies that while the methods differ in merit, the act of waxing itself is considered a form of ritual purity (tahur), reinforcing the Shia emphasis on both physical cleanliness and spiritual purification in daily practices.

en.hubeali: One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad Bin Al Qasim, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from yusuf Bin Al Sukht Al Basry, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Ibrahim Bin Yahya Bin Abu Al Balaad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Mihran, altogether from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour who said,

‘We were at Al-Medina, so Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. So I said, ‘Shaving it is preferable’, and Zurara said, ‘Plucking it is preferable’. So we both sought permission to (see) Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> permitted for us and he<sup>asws</sup> was in the bathhouse waxing, having waxed his<sup>asws</sup> armpits. So I said to Zurara, ‘Do it suffice for you?’ He said, ‘No, perhaps he<sup>asws</sup> has done this and it is not allowed for me that I do it’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘In what (discussion) are you?’ So I said, ‘Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking of the armpit and the shaving of it’. So I said that shaving is preferable, and he said plucking is preferable’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You have hit the Sunnah and Zurara has erred. Shaving it is preferable than plucking it, and waxing it is preferable than shaving it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said to us both: ‘Get waxing done’. So we both said, ‘We did that three (days) ago’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Repeat it, for waxing is a cleanser’.
en.sarwar: 5. Certain persons of our people has narrated from ibn Jumhur from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht al-Basriy from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn abu al-Balad from al-Flassan ibn Ali ibn Mehran all from ‘Abd Allah ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following: “

Once in al-Madinah Zurarah argued about pulling out or shaving of the hairs of the underarms and I said that shaving is better. Zurarah said pulling out is better. We then asked permission to meet abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. Permission was granted and he (the Imam) was in the bathhouse applying lime paste and it was applied to his underarms. I said to Zurarah that that is sufficient but Zurarah said, ‘Perhaps he (the Imam) has done so because it is not permissible for me to do so.’

He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is the issue between you two?’ I said, ‘Zurarah argues with me about the pulling up of the hairs of underarms or shaving. I say that shaving is better than pulling it out and he says pulling out is better.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You have followed the Sunnah correctly but Zurarah has missed it. Shaving is better than pulling out and applying lime paste is better than shaving.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Apply lime paste.’ We said that we had done so three days ago. He (the Imam) said, ‘Apply it again; it is a cleanser.’”
